TS-F01.title: Mathematical reasoning and proof
core_concepts: Translate English claims into quantified statements; negate precisely; identify hidden assumptions and counterexamples.
Choose proof strategy from logical form; distinguish definition expansion from theorem invocation; write readable proofs.
Use counterexamples, induction, functions/inverses, and invariant-style reasoning.
TS-F01.exit_capability: Own definitions, quantifiers, implication, counterexample, induction and proof structure.
TS-F01.deletion_reason: Without quantifiers, counterexamples and proof, specifications cannot distinguish testing from necessity.

journey.title: Mathematical reasoning and proof
journey.question: When does an argument establish a claim, rather than merely make it plausible?
journey.first_attempt: Negate 'Every tested component is safe.' Give an example where many successful tests fail to establish safety. Explain the missing inference.

TS-F02.title: Calculus + vector calculus
core_concepts: Interpret limits as local behavior; reason about continuity and approximation rather than symbolic manipulation only.
Treat derivatives as local linear maps/rates; connect geometry, units, sensitivity and dynamics.
Linearize nonlinear systems, formulate local sensitivity, and use derivatives for optimization/root finding.
Treat integration as accumulation/conservation; connect rates to stocks and local to global quantities.
Represent geometry, motion, forces and trajectories in 3D; manipulate dot/cross products and vector kinematics.
Own gradient, directional derivative, Jacobian, multiple integrals, flux/circulation and divergence/curl intuition.
TS-F02.exit_capability: Own limits, derivatives as local linearization, integrals as accumulation, gradients/Jacobians, line/surface integrals and field theorems.
TS-F02.deletion_reason: Without local linearization and accumulation, continuous physical models and their approximations cannot be reconstructed.
TS-F02.gate: Reconstruct -> transfer -> break -> bound -> check -> defend

TS-F03.title: Linear algebra
core_concepts: Represent state/data as vectors; use norms, inner products, angles and linear maps.
Diagnose redundancy, basis choice, rank and matrix-as-map thinking.
Solve linear systems; reason about reachability over repeated matrix dynamics; interpret inverses and condition.
Derive least squares as projection; understand residual orthogonality and regression geometry.
Handle constraints, nonlinear fitting, SVD/eigenstructure, low-rank approximation and ill-conditioning.
TS-F03.exit_capability: Own vector spaces, projections, least squares, matrix maps, rank/nullspace, conditioning, SVD and eigenstructure.
TS-F03.deletion_reason: Without rank, projection and conditioning, inverse problems and multivariate models hide non-identifiability.
TS-F03.gate: Reconstruct -> transfer -> break -> bound -> check -> defend

TS-F04.title: ODEs + dynamical systems
core_concepts: Translate verbal rate laws into ODEs; solve and interpret first-order models and equilibrium behavior.
Analyze oscillators, characteristic roots, transient/steady response and resonance.
Represent coupled state dynamics; connect eigenstructure to modes and stability.
Analyze nonlinear equilibria, local stability, phase portraits and bifurcation-style qualitative changes.
Recognize timescale separation, nonlinear feedback, bifurcation and chaotic sensitivity.
TS-F04.exit_capability: Translate changing systems into state equations; solve and analyze equilibria, stability, oscillation, nonlinear behavior and feedback.
TS-F04.deletion_reason: Without state evolution, equilibria and stability, feedback and time-dependent physical systems become opaque.
TS-F04.gate: Reconstruct -> transfer -> break -> bound -> check -> defend

TS-F05.title: Probability
core_concepts: Define sample spaces/events; count without over/undercounting; move between symmetry stories and formal probability.
Update beliefs with evidence; use total probability/Bayes; distinguish independence from mutual exclusivity.
Model uncertainty with random variables; exploit linearity of expectation; reason with variance and indicators.
Work with densities, Normal/Exponential models, covariance/correlation, joint/marginal/conditional distributions.
Transform variables, condition on information, use bounds/LLN/CLT and know approximation regimes.
TS-F05.exit_capability: Quantify uncertainty, conditioning, expectation, dependence, transformations, concentration and asymptotics.
TS-F05.deletion_reason: Without conditional probability and distributions, uncertain evidence cannot support calibrated decisions.

TS-F06.deletion_reason: Without estimands, confounding and uncertainty, observational association is mistaken for intervention effects.

SRC-HW-LEG-002.boundary: Treat tactics as hypotheses to test, not universal laws.

SRC-HW-LEG-003.title: How to Talk to Anyone
SRC-HW-LEG-003.use: Use as a drill bank for initiating, sustaining, and closing interactions.
SRC-HW-LEG-003.boundary: Do not treat a tactic's memorable presentation as evidence of causal generality.

SRC-HW-LEG-004.title: Influence, New and Expanded
SRC-HW-LEG-004.use: Study influence principles as recurrent mechanisms and boundary-sensitive heuristics.
SRC-HW-LEG-004.boundary: Mechanisms vary by context; persuasion is not evidence that a claim is true.

SRC-HW-LEG-005.author_or_authority: Douglas Stone, Bruce Patton & Sheila Heen
SRC-HW-LEG-005.title: Difficult Conversations
SRC-HW-LEG-005.use: Practice separating stories, feelings/identity stakes, and learning-oriented conversation.
SRC-HW-LEG-005.boundary: Not a substitute for structural power analysis.

SRC-HW-LEG-006.title: The Strategy of Conflict
SRC-HW-LEG-006.use: Focus on commitment, credible threats/promises, focal points, bargaining, timing, and information.
SRC-HW-LEG-006.boundary: Formal elegance does not guarantee empirical fit.

SRC-HW-LEG-007.title: Micromotives and Macrobehavior
SRC-HW-LEG-007.use: Focus on how individually reasonable choices can generate unintended aggregate patterns.
SRC-HW-LEG-007.boundary: Do not assume simple local rules explain every macro pattern.

SRC-HW-LEG-008.title: The Evolution of Cooperation
SRC-HW-LEG-008.use: Study repeated Prisoner's Dilemma, reciprocity, retaliation, forgiveness, and the shadow of the future.
SRC-HW-LEG-008.boundary: Tournament success is not a universal prescription for real institutions.

SRC-HW-LEG-009.title: The Strength of Weak Ties
SRC-HW-LEG-009.use: Study bridges between micro interaction and macro diffusion, mobility, and community organization.
SRC-HW-LEG-009.boundary: Network association alone does not identify causal influence.

SRC-HW-LEG-010.title: The Logic of Collective Action
SRC-HW-LEG-010.use: Study why shared interests do not automatically create organized collective action.
SRC-HW-LEG-010.boundary: Compare its predictions with institutions that successfully govern collective problems.

SRC-HW-LEG-011.title: Governing the Commons
SRC-HW-LEG-011.use: Study rules-in-use, monitoring, sanctions, local knowledge, and institutional diversity in commons governance.
SRC-HW-LEG-011.boundary: Design principles are context-dependent, not formulas.

SRC-HW-LEG-012.title: Economy and Society (selected sections on bureaucracy and authority)
SRC-HW-LEG-012.use: Study legal-rational authority, office, hierarchy, rules, and bureaucratic organization.
SRC-HW-LEG-012.boundary: Ideal types are analytic tools, not literal descriptions of every organization.

SRC-HW-LEG-013.title: Formal Models of Bureaucracy
SRC-HW-LEG-013.use: Study delegation, expertise, information asymmetry, bureaucratic hierarchy, and agency dilemmas.
SRC-HW-LEG-013.boundary: Formal models require explicit assumptions and institutional context.

SRC-HW-LEG-014.title: Power: A Radical View
SRC-HW-LEG-014.use: Study decision, agenda, preference-shaping, domination, and consent as competing dimensions of power.
SRC-HW-LEG-014.boundary: Do not collapse every social influence into an unfalsifiable power claim.

SRC-HW-LEG-015.title: Authority
SRC-HW-LEG-015.use: Use to distinguish de facto power from authority and normative legitimacy.
SRC-HW-LEG-015.boundary: Philosophical legitimacy and empirical acceptance are different questions.

SRC-HW-LEG-016.title: U.S. Constitution + Constitution Annotated
SRC-HW-LEG-016.use: Learn the structural allocation of legislative, executive, judicial, federal, state, and rights-related authority.
SRC-HW-LEG-016.boundary: Constitutional text is not identical to current doctrine; use annotations for interpretation.

SRC-HW-LEG-017.title: Federalist No. 10 and No. 51
SRC-HW-LEG-017.use: Study faction, extended republic, separation of powers, and checks-and-balances design logic.
SRC-HW-LEG-017.boundary: Treat as arguments by advocates of ratification, not neutral descriptions of all later practice.

SRC-HW-LEG-018.author_or_authority: Congressional Research Service / Library of Congress
SRC-HW-LEG-018.title: Constitution Annotated: Separation of Powers & Federalism
SRC-HW-LEG-018.use: Use for current structural exposition of separation of powers and federalism.
SRC-HW-LEG-018.boundary: A reference map is not a substitute for case-specific legal research.

SRC-HW-LEG-019.title: American Government 4e (public opinion, elections, parties, interest groups, media)
SRC-HW-LEG-019.use: Use for a current structural scaffold of U.S. political intermediation.
SRC-HW-LEG-019.boundary: Textbook simplification should be supplemented with primary data for live controversies.

SRC-HW-LEG-020.title: Introduction to Sociology 3e, Chapter 9: Social Stratification
SRC-HW-LEG-020.use: Build clean distinctions among class, wealth, income, status, mobility, ideology, and stratification.
SRC-HW-LEG-020.boundary: Definitions and examples are scaffolding; empirical magnitudes change over time.

SRC-HW-LEG-021.title: The Logic of Collective Action (concentrated vs diffuse interests)
SRC-HW-LEG-021.use: Apply organization costs and benefit concentration to distributional politics.
SRC-HW-LEG-021.boundary: Do not infer political outcomes from concentration alone.

SRC-HW-LEG-022.title: Open Frontier Curriculum: Human-systems reference map
SRC-HW-LEG-022.use: Use its separation of source roles and its reconstruct-transfer-break-bound-check-defend mastery cycle.
SRC-HW-LEG-022.boundary: This workbook is an original synthesis, not an official extension of the repository.
